Cc: James Bell <james.bell@medicore.net>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy questions: BYOK, operator access, and logs

Irene — thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed with procurement, our security team has a couple of gating questions about the private deployment model you discussed (on-prem + isolated VPC):

1) Key ownership: we need to confirm that the customer-managed key model truly means our CMK (HSM-backed) is the only key that can decrypt inference payloads and logs. Is there ever a path where Redwood would have a copy/escrow of that key?

2) Operator visibility: your slides mention an \"operator\" role. Can you define what telemetry/logs Redwood operators can see in a private deploy (control plane vs data plane)? We need to insure PHI-containing inference payloads are never viewable in plain text by any Redwood personnel.

3) Break-glass & forensics: in the event of a support incident, what is your break-glass flow? Who approves, what audit is recorded, and can we require joint custody for any emergency key use?

4) Cross-border/data transfer: our legal team wants confirmation that operator tooling/engineering access is limited to US-only hosts unless we explicitly permit otherwise.

Please respond with the minimum-privilege design and any suggested contract language or annex wording we should include in the DPA.

Thanks — Samira
Security Lead, HearthHealth

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai

Samira — great questions, thank you. I want to make sure we answer precisely and capture proposed contract language for your DPA. I'm copying engineering and privacy to finalize the technical controls. High-level answers below; internal detail and annex draft to follow by EOD tomorrow.

- Key ownership: Redwood does not retain customer key material for decrypting inference payloads in a BYOK private deployment. We support customer-managed CMKs in both cloud KMS (Cloud HSM) and on-prem HSM integrations. We can add a clause that expressly disallows key escrow or key export by Redwood.

- Operator visibility: Our recommended architecture splits the control plane (managed by Redwood for orchestration) from the data plane (deployed in your VPC/on-prem). Only aggregated telemetry from the data plane (metrics, health checks, token counts) is exported unless you opt-in to more detailed logs. Plaintext inference payloads are never exported to Redwood-managed control plane storage.

- Break-glass: We have a documented emergency access workflow. Any operator elevation requires a customer-designated approver, an auditable ticket, and automated session recording. We can offer joint-custody (two-person approval) for critical key operations as an addendum.

- Cross-border: We will commit operator tooling/engineering interactions to US-only unless you authorize other regions; we can include this in the DPA and SOW.

Next steps: Prashant (engineering) will outline exact telemetry fields and redaction options, Priyom will draft the BYOK annex wording, and I will compile proposed DPA language for your legal team.

Attached: initial network segmentation sketch and an example BYOK annex outline.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Legal — Redwood Inference

Irene — notes from implementation side; pinging Karthik for any legal/timing constraints.

1) BYOK technical model:
- Data plane holds runtime keys encrypted with the CMK you supply. Decryption happens only within your tenant hosts (VMs/containers) using the HSM or cloud KMS you control. Redwood never has an unenveloped copy.
- For on-prem HSMs, we support PKCS#11 integration; for cloud we use CMEK patterns where the CMK wraps per-tenant data keys.

2) Operator roles & telemetry:
- Control plane (Redwood-managed): scheduling, routing metadata, quota enforcement. Telemetry exported: service-level metrics (cpu/mem, request counts, anonymized error codes).
- Data plane (customer-managed): inference inputs/outputs remain in your network. We ship an agent that only exposes the following by default: heartbeats, node health, tokenized request counts.
- Optional: redacted logs for debugging. Redaction levels: header-only, hashed-payload, or full (customer opt-in).

3) Break-glass & forensics:
- Recommended flow: (a) Customer raises ticket in their Jira instance with mandatory approver; (b) Redwood opens ephemeral support session; (c) All commands are recorded and stored in your encrypted audit bucket.
- For forensic decryption: we can implement a joint-custody flow using your HSM's two-person policy or a Redwood multi-sig approval, but only if the customer signs the annex.

4) Data residency & operator access:
- We will restrict operator console access to US IP ranges on request and log all operator sessions (including bastion hops) to an auditable feed you control.

I'll prepare a terse annex draft (BYOK + operator visibility matrix) and a checklist for your security team. Laura, please add the SLA/exception language we discussed last quarter.

— Priyom
Staff Engineer, Private Deployments

Samira / James — following up with the proposed package and ask for quick alignment so procurement can move forward. Summary and asks below.

Summary of commitments (to be included as an annex to the DPA / SOW):
- Key custody: Redwood will not escrow, export, or hold a copy of customer CMKs. Customer CMKs (cloud KMS or on-prem HSM) will be required for decryption of any inference payloads.
- Telemetry & logs: Default exports are aggregated metrics and node health. Plaintext inference payloads will not be transmitted to Redwood control plane. Any redacted logs for debugging require explicit opt-in and will be bound by an additional access policy.
- Emergency access: Break-glass will require a customer-designated approver, an auditable ticket, and session recording. We propose joint-custody using your HSM two-person rule for any forensic decryption and can add explicit language in the annex.
- Operator region restrictions: Redwood will restrict operator tooling to US-only IP ranges unless you provide written consent for other regions.

Attachments: I am attaching our BYOK annex draft and the network diagram. Please review and flag any wording changes after which we'll produce a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Action items for HearthHealth:
1) Confirm you want the joint-custody two-person rule for break-glass. (Yes/No)
2) Confirm desired redaction level for debug logs (header-only / hashed-payload / full-optin).
3) Confirm procurement timeline so we can lock the SOW dates.

If it's easier, we can do a 30-minute call to walk through the annex tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Legal — Redwood Inference
